title: How to Use AI to Write Code Faster (Without Breaking Things)
hook: Most developers use AI coding tools completely wrong, and it costs them hours.

narration.text: Most developers use AI coding tools completely wrong, and it costs them hours. The fix is simpler than you think.
Tools like GitHub Copilot and Cursor can write code for you in seconds. But if you just accept whatever they generate, bugs pile up fast.
The first rule is to give context, not just commands. Instead of typing 'write a login function', describe the inputs, the expected output, and any constraints.
The more specific your prompt, the less the AI has to guess. Guessing is where errors come from.
Second, always ask the AI to explain what it just wrote. If it cannot explain it clearly, the code probably has a flaw.
Third, work in small chunks. Ask for one function at a time, test it, then move on. Generating hundreds of lines at once makes debugging a nightmare.
You can also paste error messages directly into the chat. Tools like ChatGPT and Claude are surprisingly good at diagnosing what went wrong.
The developers saving the most time treat AI as a junior colleague, not a magic button. You still need to review the output.
Start with one tool, learn its limits, and build from there. GitHub Copilot is a solid first step if you are already inside an editor.
AI will not replace good coding habits. But it will make those habits much faster to act on.

description: AI coding tools can save you hours every week, but only if you use them correctly. This video covers the practical habits that stop AI-generated code from introducing bugs and breaking your projects. Apply these principles from day one and you will get reliable results far sooner.
